name: Manikaran Sahib Gurudwara Langar
signature_dish: rice cooked in geothermal hot springs
dress_code: head covered, shoes off, no leather
why_it_matters: Where Sikh tradition says Bhai Mardana lifted a stone at Guru Nanak's instruction and a hot spring burst forth — chapatis floated cooked when prayed over. The langar still cooks rice the same way: muslin pots dipped into the boiling spring, no fire. Free, 24/7, served to anyone who covers their head and sits on the floor.
insider_tip: Rice is the dish to ask about — it's the one cooked directly in the spring water in cloth bundles. Volunteer for sewa in the kitchen for an hour and you'll see the bundles pulled out steaming.
signature_address: Gurudwara Sri Manikaran Sahib, Manikaran, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Lord Ramchandra Temple Langar
dress_code: shoes off, head covered for prasad area
why_it_matters: Built in the 17th century by Kullu's Raja Jagat Singh — older than the Gurudwara. The temple complex has 40 pilgrim rooms, twin hot-spring kunds (Sita and Rama), and runs its own langar so Hindu pilgrims can eat satvik food cooked the same geothermal way. Quieter than the Gurudwara hall.
insider_tip: Sit through aarti before lunch — the langar opens straight after, and the queue is half the size of the Gurudwara's. Donate at the daan box on your way out; the meal is free but the temple runs on offerings.
signature_address: Lord Ramchandra Temple, Manikaran Bazaar, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Manikaran Bazaar Tea & Samosa Stalls
why_it_matters: The narrow lane between the Gurudwara and the Shiva temple is lined with tin-roof stalls selling adrak chai, fresh jalebis, and steaming samosas to pilgrims. Nothing is plated — you stand, you eat, you watch the Parvati roar past. This is the Manikaran food experience outside the langars.
insider_tip: Jalebis are best mid-morning when the kadhai oil is fresh; by afternoon the syrup gets thick. Pair one with ginger chai — the cold off the river makes both taste better than they have any right to.
signature_address: Manikaran Bazaar (between Gurudwara Manikaran Sahib and Shiv Mandir), Manikaran 175105

name: Hotel Parvati Valley Restaurant
why_it_matters: One of the few hotel restaurants in Manikaran with proper sit-down service and room service — the alternative when the Gurudwara hall is at peak-pilgrim crush. 24-year-old property near the Gurudwara; the kitchen does standard North Indian and Himachali rajma-chawal at honest prices.
insider_tip: Ask for a table on the side facing the Parvati if you can — the river is loud but the view of the gorge is the reason to skip the langar for a meal here. Skip the Chinese; stick to rajma-chawal or thali.
signature_address: Hotel Parvati Valley, Near Gurudwara Sahib, Manikaran 175105
